tools.name: convert_script
tools.description: Rewrites text from one Indian script into another letter by letter, e.g. Devanagari 'नमस्ते' → Kannada 'ನಮಸ್ತೇ'. The language does not change, only the letters. Works between the Brahmic scripts (Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam) and Meetei Mayek; soun

tools.name: get_keymap
tools.description: Returns the phonetic keyboard map for a language: which Latin keys produce each letter. Useful for teaching someone to type a language or for building correct romanised input for transliterate.

tools.name: list_languages
tools.description: Lists the 22 scheduled languages of India (plus extra official scripts for Kashmiri, Manipuri and Sindhi) with the codes the other tools accept.

tools.name: native_digits
tools.description: Replaces ASCII digits 0-9 with a language's native digits, e.g. '2026' → '२०२६' (Hindi), '௨௦௨௬' (Tamil), '۲۰۲۶' (Urdu).

tools.name: translate
tools.description: Translates the meaning of text between English and the 22 scheduled languages of India, or between two of them, e.g. 'Where is the station?' → 'स्टेशन कहाँ है?' (Hindi). English → Indic uses AI4Bharat IndicTrans2; Indic → English uses Gemma 4; Indic → Indic goes through English. Free use: up to 2,00

tools.name: transliterate
tools.description: Writes romanised (Latin-letter) text in an Indian script by sound, e.g. 'namaste' → 'नमस्ते' for Hindi or 'vaNakkam' → 'வணக்கம்' for Tamil. This is transliteration, not translation: spell the words as they sound in the target language. Keys follow ITRANS/Baraha conventions: capitals for long vowels
